newsitem.title: BRUNEI: Japanese PM to kick off ASEAN trip in Brunei.
newsitem.headline: Japanese PM to kick off ASEAN trip in Brunei.

text.p: Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto will kick off his five-nation Southeast Asian trip with a one-day stop in tiny Brunei on Tuesday, before proceeding across the South China Sea to Malaysia.

Officials in oil-rich Brunei, which shares the island of Borneo with the Malaysian states of Sabah and Sarawak, said Hashimoto was expected to arrive at Banda airport at 5:20 p.m. local time (0920 GMT).

During the visit, Hashimoto will meet with Brunei's Sultan Sir Hassanal Bolkiah, who is also prime minister and absolute ruler of the country. Hashimoto is due to leave the capital, Bandar Seri Begawan, on Wednesday morning for Kuala Lumpur.

The Japanese leader, who is visiting five members of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) over eight days, aims to bolster Japan's ties with the region and muster support for its foreign policy initiatives.
"The ASEAN countries, positioned as the core of the Asia-Pacific region, have joined hands with Japan in the past," Hashimoto said on Saturday. "I would like to deepen that relationship."
In addition to Brunei and Malaysia, Hashimoto is also visiting Singapore, Indonesia and Vietnam. He visited the other two ASEAN members, Thailand and the Philippines, last year.
The prime minister's visit to the region had been in doubt after a hostage crisis erupted at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, Peru last month.
But Hashimoto said he would go ahead with the trip to signal his confidence in the Peruvian government's handling of the crisis. Marxist rebels still hold 74 hostages in the 19-day-old standoff.

In a sign of official concern about the crisis, reporters covering Hashimoto's visit to Kuala Lumpur were told by Malaysian officials to arrive at least 40 minutes early to undergo increased security checks.

Hashimoto is due to land in the Malaysian capital on Wednesday at 10:45 a.m. local (0245 GMT). He is scheduled to meet with Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and has an audience with Malaysia's King Ja'afar Tuanku Abdul Rahman.
He will also visit parliament on Wednesday afternoon.
An official at Malaysia's Foreign Ministry said Hashimoto's visit to the region was to "enhance bilateral relations". Hashimoto leaves Kuala Lumpur on Thursday morning for Jakarta.
Hashimoto's Asia-Pacific strategy is expected to be underpinned by increasing economic cooperation with ASEAN countries and containing China's growing influence in the region.
